prompt: More and more people are reading news online, but newspapers are still the main source of news for most people. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that although an increasing number of people now read the news online, newspapers remain the primary source of information for the majority of the public. I disagree with this view to a large extent, as digital platforms have become far more convenient, accessible and up to date than printed newspapers.

The main reason why online news has become dominant is convenience. People can access news instantly through smartphones, tablets and computers, regardless of where they are. Unlike newspapers, which must be bought or delivered, online articles can be read at any time and are often free. In addition, digital platforms allow readers to follow breaking news as it happens. For example, during elections, natural disasters or major international events, websites and social media platforms can update information within minutes, while newspapers can only report the story the following day.

Another important factor is that younger generations are much less likely to rely on printed newspapers. Many people now receive news through search engines, news apps and social media feeds, where stories are often personalised according to their interests. This makes online news more attractive than traditional newspapers, which provide the same content to every reader. Furthermore, online sources often include videos, interviews, live updates and links to related articles, making the news experience more interactive and informative.

However, it is true that newspapers still play an important role for some groups, particularly older people who are more comfortable with printed material. Newspapers may also be seen as more reliable than some online sources, especially because the internet contains misinformation and poorly verified content. Nevertheless, this does not mean that newspapers are still the main source of news for most people.

In conclusion, while newspapers continue to be valued by certain readers, I strongly disagree that they remain the dominant source of news. The speed, accessibility and convenience of online platforms have made them the preferred choice for the majority of people today.
